A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Deliberation on Priors (DP) framework. Their complete 22-page contents, including equations, tables, figures and Technical Appendices A–B, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original KGQA benchmark results, component ablations, error analyses, exemplar sensitivity experiments and case studies in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds measurements of backtracking frequency in Section 4.5.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same shortest-path supervision, SFT and KTO training, perturbations, path selection, instantiation and constraint-triggered backtracking. New Section 4.5 measures the existing backtracking mechanism without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebQSP and CWQ over Freebase and MetaQA movie questions spanning one to three hops. The added comparisons and backtracking analysis use retained WebQSP/CWQ coverage without introducing another task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds vanilla zero-shot ChatGPT, GPT-4 and LLaMA3.1-8B comparisons on WebQSP and CWQ. All previous SL, ICL and HL comparators remain; the separate standalone GPT-4.1 ablation in Table 3 is also retained.

E3.justification: The added vanilla comparisons specify a zero-shot condition, and Section 4.5 introduces average backtracking steps per test question as a diagnostic measure. Existing test sample sizes, H/H@1/F1 metrics, training budgets and few-shot settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 4.5 and Table 5 examine how frequently DP backtracks with GPT-3.5 versus GPT-4.1 on two datasets. Existing component ablations, error analyses, exemplar sensitivity experiments, interaction analyses and appendix success/failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports standard deviations for DP with GPT-4 in Table 2. The deviations for the other four DP configurations were already reported in v1 Appendix B.3, Table 7, and are retained in v2 Table 8. The stated three-run count is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds zero-shot results, including GPT-4 H@1/F1 of 67.4/49.5 on WebQSP and 50.8/46.1 on CWQ. New Table 5 reports GPT-3.5/GPT-4.1 backtracking averages of 0.10/0.42 on CWQ and 0.07/0.21 on WebQSP. Previously reported means and appendix findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5) retain their substance. Section 3.1 removes the redundant inline domain/codomain notation for M while preserving its question-to-path-set description and construction. No assumptions, proofs or theoretical results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about trustworthy reasoning through structural and constraint priors, state-of-the-art performance, flexibility and efficiency. The abstract's claimed 13% CWQ Hit@1 improvement is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds commentary about vanilla LLM instability and DP's lower variance. Section 4.5 tentatively attributes GPT-4.1's more frequent backtracking to stronger instruction following and stricter constraint checking, linking this to reasoning quality. Existing limitations and appendix failure interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendices B.1–B.2 retain the same hardware, precision, LoRA configuration, learning rates, training epochs and prompt exemplars. Code and model/framework access information is unchanged; the added analyses supply no additional implementation instructions.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Appendix A preserves the positioning against retrieval and relation-path approaches, including the claimed novelty of using constraint priors in reasoning.

P1.justification: Limited grammar and notation edits and updated venue/funding text accompany a short new Backtracking Analysis subsection and additions to results commentary. The former Section 4.5 becomes Section 4.6; the broader narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 adds vanilla rows and uncertainty values in a smaller, denser layout. V2 adds backtracking Table 5, relocates the efficiency table within page 9 and renumbers subsequent tables. The conclusion and references reflow, while all figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added zero-shot controls and backtracking measurements improve empirical context, while newly reported GPT-4 standard deviations fill a limited reporting gap. Existing experiments and appendices remain intact. The instruction-following explanation is not isolated experimentally, and Table 2 becomes denser, but the additional evidence and transparency provide a modest overall benefit.
